triggerdupe.name: Triggerdupe
triggerdupe.creator: Human#6606
triggerdupe.content: Since some entities (like the statue test dummies found in Holy Mountains) are considered to be both enemies and physics objects, trigger spells that hit them will activate twice, potentially giving players an overinflated idea of the damage that their wands output.

tablet.name: tablet
tablet.creator: GrahamBurger#2747
tablet.content:
Tablets have a projectile component that can hit enemies, and also physics damage depending on how fast they're moving. If the projectile component hits an enemy, it will be attributed to you and won't cause trick kills.
if you throw a tablet by clicking and dragging it out of your inventory, the projectile component won't know it was thrown by you and will cause trick kills every time. (Or you can just chuck it really fast, which will make it cause trick kills moderately more often due to the physics damage hitting / killing first.)

kickparry.name: kickparry
kickparry.creator: GrahamBurger#2747
kickparry.content: The elusive kick-parry... yep, that's a real game mechanic! Kicking with very precise timing can allow you to reflect melee-type damage back onto the attacker. This works even with ranged melee attacks, like tentacles or the tongue of a <:entity_konna_large:740666473927934123>. It's not too practical, but hey, it's fun!

progress.name: progress
progress.creator: Human#6606
progress.content:
The progress menu is split into three sections:
**Perks**
> All perks are unlocked by default, picking one up will add it to your progress log if you haven’t taken it yet. Observant eyes might notice, not all perks are so easy to add though; ||they require a little more searching…||
**Spells**
> As with perks, casting a spell will add it to your progress menu, and unlock it if you haven’t already, though spells you haven’t unlocked won’t spawn normally. Not all spells are unlocked by default, and you will have to complete incredible feats of magic and knowledge to uncover them!
**Enemies**
> Last of all, when you slay an enemy, and *only* when you slay it yourself\* (trick kills won’t count!) it will be added to the progress menu\*\*, displaying how many times you’ve killed it, and how many times it’s killed you. 

\* Some exceptions may apply (||The boss will always be a kill on your part||)
\*\* One specific enemy counts as two entries, meaning it is possible to get over 100% of the progress menu, though it’s up to you to find out who!

mods.name: mods
mods.creator: nathanskimscam
mods.content:
Some things are disabled if you have any mods enabled during a run. (The daily practice mode and nightmare mode count as mods for this purpose.) Notably, **you can still get unlocks and ||achievement pillars|| during modded runs**. Generally, the only things that are disabled by mods are:
- Steam achievements
- End screen stats being saved after winning a run
- Wands being saved in the bones folder for<:entity_player_ghost_kummitus:970573426777546802>
- "The Gods Are Afraid" / "Very Curious" messages for dealing over 1 million damage and reaching negative HP, respectively
- The ||Cauldron|| or ||Eyes|| secrets appearing
The https://discord.com/channels/453998283174576133/1020458521927630879 or https://discord.com/channels/453998283174576133/1177451453086974063 mods allows you to play modded runs without these restrictions, if you'd like.

spellspawns.name: spellspawns
spellspawns.creator: noby_y
spellspawns.content:
## Wands:
Naturally generated wands spawn with spells __1 tier lower__ than the wand's tier limited to spell types: **Projectile | Modifier | Multicast | Static Projectile** (but only as an Always Cast). Projectile type spells have a repeatable 10% chance to advance in tier

Exceptions: [Unique wands](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/Wands#Unique_wands>) | [Pre-made wands](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/Wand_and_Spell_Tiers#Wands_(premade)>)
## Other sources:
If you're looking for spells of different types you can find them in: [Holy Mountain / biome spell shops](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/Wand_and_Spell_Tiers#Biomes>) | ||Hell / Sky|| shops ([T10 spells](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/Wand_and_Spell_Tiers#Tier_10_Spells>) only)

These places will not care about spell tiers and spawn probabilities: ||[Eye rooms](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Hourglass_Chamber#Teleportatium>)|| | [Treasure Chests](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/Treasure_Chest#Loot_Table>) | [Utility boxes](<https://noita.wiki.gg/wiki/Utility_Box>) (only Modifier and Utility type spells) | ||Gate guardian|| boss loot

backup.name: backup
backup.creator: noby_y
backup.content:
## How to make a backup
### 1\. Go to your save folder (make sure the game is closed)
**Windows:**
- `%localappdata%low/Nolla_Games_Noita/`
**Linux:**
- `~/.steam/steam/steamapps/compatdata/881100/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/LocalLow/Nolla_Games_Noita/`
- `~/.wine/drive_c/users/[your_username]/AppData/LocalLow/Nolla_Games_Noita/`
`[your_username]` - your account's username (e.g., `users/god_gamer_69/AppData`)
### 2. Copy your save folder
`save00` is your main save folder (ignore the rest). Copy `save00` to a different folder or maybe even to the same folder and rename it into something like `backup_1`.
## How to restore to a backup
1. Go to your save folder (see above)
- Delete `save00` (current save)
- Paste back the backup folder (make sure the folder is named `save00` )
- Open Noita and continue playing

multiplayer.name: multiplayer
multiplayer.creator: nathanskimscam
multiplayer.content:
Noita has no built-in multiplayer options in vanilla, but there are several options to choose from with the help of mods!
- [**Noita Entangled Worlds**](https://github.com/IntQuant/noita_entangled_worlds) lets you have a true online multiplayer experience, complete with world sync! You can join their discord here: <https://discord.gg/S7QdV8ZZPw>
- [**Noita Arena**](https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=3035468502) lets you fight your friends (and foes) in an online round-based PvP arena! Build wands and duke it out against other players! You can join their discord here: <https://discord.gg/zJyUSHGcme>
- [**Iota Multplayer**](https://discord.com/channels/453998283174576133/1262257753636864091/1262257753636864091) lets you play couch co-op with a friend! Simple, but very fun!
- [**Noita Together**](https://github.com/Noita-Together/noita-together) lets you play with other players on the same seed! You're each in separate worlds, but you can trade items and gold between players, and see where other players are in their own worlds.

healingdamage.name: healingdamage
healingdamage.creator: grahamburger
healingdamage.content:
When it comes to projectiles like Healing Bolt and Circle of Vigour, their healing effect is not just *negative damage*; they use a special **Healing** damage type. While most damage types cannot effectively go below 0, healing damage cannot effectively go *above* 0. 
Note that you can still make healing spells deal damage by, for example, adding <:spell_damage:888282935306899476> to it, because Damage Plus adds *projectile* damage. The healing effect is still there, it just is overshadowed by the damage added. If you're having trouble healing because you took Concentrated Spells or Boomerang Spells, try using a modifier like Piercing to reduce its projectile damage to 0. The healing will stay!
TLDR: You can't make Healing Bolt heal you more by reducing its projectile damage.

stevaristatue.name: stevaristatue
stevaristatue.creator: atomguy
stevaristatue.content:
It's very common that enough damage to the holy mountain will anger the gods in your runs, which inevitably will lead to the Stevari (AKA Steve, mall cop) spawning and causing you some trouble. Fortunately, the holy mountain comes equipped with just the thing for him: the statues!

There are 2 extremely reliable statue kick methods which you can use in every run you play.

The one you'll likely use first utilises the statue found at the right, first kick the statue so that it's base is facing right as shown in the clip below (1st gif)

And as soon as he's about to be on top of your head, kick the statue directly up! It should look like this (2nd gif)

The left statue can also be utilised. First you'll need to pay Steve a visit to let him know you're there (3rd gif)
He'll soon start to chase you at which point you can make your way over to the left while Steve is focused on the fish, stand against the back of the statue, wait for Steve to come right over the top of you and once again, kick the statue directly up! It should look like this (4th gif)

hmescapes.name: hmescapes
hmescapes.creator: pudy248
hmescapes.content: There are a few common strategies to safely bypass the holy mountain collapse trigger (see .hmtrigger for specifics). Aside from using polymorph or teleporting out of the mountain directly, here are the most common strategies. Return inside of a trigger can also be used in place of standard teleport bolts.

shotstate.name: shotstate
shotstate.creator: noby_y
shotstate.content:
### There's only 2 ways to separate modifications from projectiles:
- Separate wand casts (clicks)
- Triggers
### When looking at a wand ask these 2 questions:
- Is the wand you're looking at casting Modifiers and projectile spells in different wand casts?
- Is there a trigger separating Modifiers and projectiles into inside/outside of its payload (some projectile is inside and some Modifier is outside)?

If the answers are **No** and **No**, then there's nothing else to separate shot states -> all modifications affect all projectiles in that same shot state __regardless of order__
### Example:
<:spell_double:631582503622279198> <:spell_spark_bolt:968527256450388019> <:spell_damage:888282935306899476>
- Both <:spell_spark_bolt:968527256450388019> and <:spell_damage:888282935306899476> are cast on the same wand cast
- No triggers separate them

incompatibility.name: incompatibility
incompatibility.creator: copis
incompatibility.content:
# Identifying incompatible mods
Some mods break other mods, and in larger modpacks, this only gets more common and hard to pinpoint. Try disabling specific mods to see if the issue is fixed.
1. Check older mods: These tend to use older API features and don't account for other mods. Anything over two years old without maintenance is a strong contender.
2. Related mods: Any mod that touches the same features. Spells not working? Check spell mods. Misplaced pixel scenes? Check map mods.
3. Complicated/larger mods: These do a lot of things, and can often change more fundamental aspects of the game. Complicated spell mods, vast enemy mods, if you can't sum up its features in a single sentence it might touch the same code as another mod.
4. Binary Search: At worst, you can brute force it if guesstimating doesn't work. 
   - Disable half of your mods, keeping the broken mod enabled (or not, if unsure)
   - If the issue is resolved, disable the other half instead. If the issue is still gone, try another half, repeat step 1
   - Once you've narrowed the mods down to half and the issue persists, only disable half of these mods. repeat step 1 on this narrowed subset.
   - You will eventually chip down the mod list to the incompatible mod(s).
# Addressing incompatible mods
Once you find the incompatibility, you can choose to disable one of the mods causing the issue, and optionally use an alternative.
It is strongly recommended that you point out this issue to the mod developer and other users, if the mod is no longer in active development or maintenance you may want to consider leaving a comment pointing the issue for other people who may have this same issue. At best someone will make a 3rd party patch, at worst, you'll save someone the hassle of finding it!

infhp.name: infhp
infhp.creator: noby_y
infhp.content:
## Inf HP comes in 2 forms
### 9,223,372,036,854,774,784+
Any value above that number will just show as ∞ in the in-game UI. It has no special interactions, it simply doesn't show the true HP value.
**CAUTION:** At really high HP %based damage can become inf and instakill you due to it being stored in a smaller-sized variable.
### ~1.8e308
Actually inf HP. You don't take damage or, to be more precise, none of the damage operations can result in your HP being lowered because of how arithmetic operations with INF work.

zerkstrat.name: zerkstrat
zerkstrat.creator: noby_y
zerkstrat.content:
**Zerkstrat** is a method of cheesing ||bridge boss|| by exploiting how he interacts with a berserked player.
### How to:
Make a small berserkium pool to the right of the podium of the|| orb room|| and summon the boss (without having the effect). Once the bridge breaks, drink some of the remaining berserkium and quickly make your way to the pool.

After that simply shoot him in-between his attacks (or during his attacks if it cant reach you).

zeroweight.name: zeroweight
zeroweight.creator: pudy248
zeroweight.content: Surprisingly, Summon Portal and Summon Swamp can spawn in chests, ||eye rooms||, and from the ||Gate Boss||! They have 0 spawn weight, so they'll never appear in shops, but those 3 places select randomly from all unlocked spells without checking their weight (unless the spells are unlockable, like Rainbow Trail). Summon Portal and Summon Swamp do not have unlock flags, so they can be found outside of their respective quests.

noitoolshifts.name: noitoolshifts
noitoolshifts.creator: pudy248
noitoolshifts.content:
Noitool's fungal shift info is a little hard to read, especially after Epilogue 2. Here's how to read them.
- Every material listed on the left gets shifted to the material on the right.
- Unless you're holding a flask, in which case the material or list of materials listed on the side with "Held Material" gets replaced with the material in the flask. (If neither side has Held Material, holding a flask doesn't do anything.)
- Unless the flask is on the right side and contains gold or divine ground, in which case the shift is the left side to the corresponding material in "Gold -> X" or "Divine Ground -> X", i.e. the example below with a flask of gold performs Acid -> Excrement. Gold is not shifted away in these cases, despite what the UI leads you to believe
- Unless the left and right sides are identical, in which case the shift rerolls to a random new one and Noitool doesn't tell you what it is.

unlocks.name: unlocks
unlocks.creator: noby_y
unlocks.content:
## Unlock flags
Whether a specific spell / thing is unlocked depends on whether you have a related unlock flag in your save file. If the right flag exists, that spell can spawn. 
The flag is typically added whenever an appropriate quest gets completed. Having a locked spell spawn by other means will also add the unlock flag
## Progress
Whenever you cast a spell it gets recorded in the Progress menu. This has 0 impact on the actual gameplay
